claim: On MCR-Bench, a real-world multi-round PR-level code review benchmark with 2,269 tasks across 5 languages, the best single LLM reviewer (Claude Haiku 4.5) only reaches F1=0.551 overall on defect detection, with recall 0.630 and precision 0.579.
stance_target: ceiling on achievable defect detection with current LLM reviewers in real-world settings
scope_conditions: 2,269 real-world multi-round PR-level code review tasks, Python/Java/JavaScript/TypeScript/C#, ground truth from actual review discussions not synthetic errors
quoted_support: mainstream LLMs exhibit only modest performance on MCR-Bench, with F1 scores largely in the low-to-medium range and the best-performing model slightly exceeding 0.55, indicating persistent challenges in defect identification and contextual reasoning under multi-round code review settings.

claim: Production-style PR-level agentic code review baselines (PR-Agent, Hybrid-Review) score even lower than general-purpose LLM reviewers on MCR-Bench, with consistently low recall, showing they struggle to capture defects whose evidence evolves across review rounds.
stance_target: existing agentic code-review tooling already solves multi-round defect detection
scope_conditions: PR-Agent and Hybrid-Review baselines evaluated on MCR-Bench defect detection task
quoted_support: both baselines achieve limited performance, with generally low F1 scores and consistently low recall. This indicates that existing PR-level review baselines still struggle to capture defects whose evidence evolves across review discussions and code revisions.

claim: LLM defect-detection performance on MCR-Bench drops for TypeScript and C# relative to Python and JavaScript, with most models experiencing a pronounced drop in recall on the former languages.
stance_target: generalizability of LLM code review across programming languages
quoted_support: Models generally achieve higher F1 scores on Python and JavaScript... For languages such as TypeScript and C#, most models experience a pronounced drop in recall, and some perform substantially worse than their overall averages.
